arxiv-2103-14657.title: From hydro to jet quenching, coalescence and hadron cascade: a coupled approach to solving the R A ​ A ⊗ v 2 R_{AA}\otimes v_{2} puzzle
arxiv-2103-14657.creator: Wenbin Zhao, Weiyao Ke, Wei Chen, Tan Luo, Xin-Nian Wang
arxiv-2103-14657.description: Abstract Hydrodynamics and jet quenching are responsible for the elliptic flow v 2 v_{2} and suppression of large transverse momentum ( p T p_{T} ) hadrons, respectively, two of the most important phenomena leading to the discovery of a strongly coupled quark-gluon plasma (QGP) in high-energy heavy-ion collisions.

arxiv-2111-15321.title: Influence of atomic modeling on electron capture and shaking processes
arxiv-2111-15321.creator: A. Andoche, L. Mouawad, P.-A. Hervieux, X. Mougeot, J. Machado, J.P. Santos
arxiv-2111-15321.description: Abstract Ongoing experimental efforts to measure with unprecedented precision electron-capture probabilities challenges the current theoretical models. The short range of the weak interaction necessitates an accurate description of the atomic structure down to the nucleus region. A recent electron-capture modeling has been modified in order to test the influence of three different atomic descriptions on the decay and shaking probabilities.

arxiv-2207-02514.title: Nuclear Many-Body Effect on Particle Emissions Following Muon Capture on Si 28 {}^{28}\mathrm{Si} and Ca 40 {}^{40}\mathrm{Ca}
arxiv-2207-02514.creator: Futoshi Minato, Tomoya Naito, Osamu Iwamoto
arxiv-2207-02514.description: Abstract Muon captures on nuclei have provided us with plenty of knowledge of nuclear properties. Recently, this reaction attracts attention in electronics, because it is argued that charged particle emissions following muon capture on silicon trigger non-negligible soft errors in memory devices.

arxiv-2208-00564.title: Quantum Adaptive Fourier Features for Neural Density Estimation Thanks: Citation : Joseph et al., Quantum Adaptive Fourier Features for Neural Density Estimation.
arxiv-2208-00564.creator: Joseph A. Gallego M, Fabio A. GonzálezMindLabUniversidad Nacional de ColombiaBogotá, Colombia {jagallegom, fagonzalezo}@unal.edu.co
arxiv-2208-00564.description: Abstract Density estimation is a fundamental task in statistics and machine learning applications. Kernel density estimation is a powerful tool for non-parametric density estimation in low dimensions; however, its performance is poor in higher dimensions. Moreover, its prediction complexity scale linearly with more training data points.

arxiv-2305-02197.title: The Volume of Healthy Red Blood Cells is Optimal for Advective Oxygen Transport in Arterioles
arxiv-2305-02197.creator: Lucas Amoudruz, Athena Economides, Petros Koumoutsakos
arxiv-2305-02197.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Lucas Amoudruz, Athena Economides, Petros Koumoutsakos. Red blood cells (RBCs) are vital for transporting oxygen from the lungs to the body’s tissues through the intricate circulatory system. They achieve this by binding and releasing oxygen molecules to the abundant hemoglobin within their cytosol. The volume of RBCs affects the amount of oxygen they can carry, yet whether this volume is optimal for transporting oxygen through the circulatory system remains an open question.

arxiv-2503-09358.title: RetSTA: An LLM-Based Approach for Standardizing Clinical Fundus Image Reports
arxiv-2503-09358.creator: Jiushen Cai, Weihang Zhang, Hanruo Liu, Ningli Wang, Huiqi Li
arxiv-2503-09358.description: Abstract Standardization of clinical reports is crucial for improving the quality of healthcare and facilitating data integration. The lack of unified standards, including format, terminology, and style, is a great challenge in clinical fundus diagnostic reports, which increases the difficulty for large language models (LLMs) to understand the data.

arxiv-2504-05403.title: A Novel Approach to Linking Histology Images with DNA Methylation
arxiv-2504-05403.creator: Manahil Raza, Muhammad Dawood, Talha Qaiser, Nasir M. Rajpoot
arxiv-2504-05403.description: Abstract DNA methylation is an epigenetic mechanism that regulates gene expression by adding methyl groups to DNA. Abnormal methylation patterns can disrupt gene expression and have been linked to cancer development. To quantify DNA methylation, specialized assays are typically used. However, these assays are often costly and have lengthy processing times, which limits their widespread availability in routine clinical practice.

arxiv-2512-18497.title: Derivation of stochastic Burgers on the line with a Dirichlet boundary condition at the origin
arxiv-2512-18497.creator: Cédric Bernardin, Ana Djurdjevac, Patrícia Gonçalves, Leander Schnee
arxiv-2512-18497.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Cédric Bernardin, Ana Djurdjevac, Patrícia Gonçalves, Leander Schnee. We analyze the equilibrium fluctuations of a Hamiltonian chain of oscillators on ℤ \mathbb{Z} with an exponential potential, perturbed by a conservative, symmetric noise. Under the canonical diffusive scaling t ↦ t ​ n 2 t\mapsto tn^{2} and an interaction strength tuned by n − 1 / 2 n^{-1/2} , the fluctuation field is known to converge to the energy solution of the stochastic Burgers equation (SBE) on the torus [ 1 ] .

arxiv-2512-25022.title: Real Riemann Surfaces: Smooth and Discrete
arxiv-2512-25022.creator: Johanna Düntsch, Felix Günther
arxiv-2512-25022.description: Abstract This paper develops a discrete theory of real Riemann surfaces based on quadrilateral cellular decompositions (quad-graphs) and a linear discretization of the Cauchy-Riemann equations. We construct a discrete analogue of an antiholomorphic involution and classify the topological types of discrete real Riemann surfaces, recovering the classical results on the number of real ovals and the separation of the surface.

pmc-10653793.title: Gene editing of SAMHD1 in macrophage-like cells reveals complex relationships between SAMHD1 phospho-regulation, HIV-1 restriction, and cellular dNTP levels
pmc-10653793.creator: Moritz Schüssler, Kerstin Schott, Nina Verena Fuchs, Adrian Oo, Morssal Zahadi, Paula Rauch, Baek Kim, Renate König
pmc-10653793.description: Sterile α motif and HD domain-containing protein 1 (SAMHD1) is a dNTP triphosphate triphosphohydrolase (dNTPase) and a potent restriction factor for immunodeficiency virus 1 (HIV-1), active in myeloid and resting CD4+ T cells. The anti-viral activity of SAMHD1 is regulated by dephosphorylation of the residue T592. However, the impact of T592 phosphorylation on dNTPase activity is still under debate.

pmc-11494867.title: Oxysterols contribute to immune cell recruitment in SLE skin lesions
pmc-11494867.creator: Xiaoyun Chen, Lianlian Ouyang, Sujie Jia, Ming Zhao
pmc-11494867.description: BackgroundAbnormal oxysterol metabolism has been observed in the peripheral blood of SLE patients, but its role in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) skin lesions remains unclear.MethodsTargeted oxidized lipid metabolomics analysis using liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) was performed to quantify oxysterols in SLE skin lesions. Immunohistochemical staining and single-cell sequencing data analysis confirmed the upregulation of oxysterol-encoding enzymes CH25H and CYP7B1.

pmc-11725321.title: CryptoBench: cryptic protein–ligand binding sites dataset and benchmark
pmc-11725321.creator: Vít Škrhák, Marian Novotný, Christos P Feidakis, Radoslav Krivák, David Hoksza
pmc-11725321.description: MotivationStructure-based methods for detecting protein–ligand binding sites play a crucial role in various domains, from fundamental research to biomedical applications. However, current prediction methodologies often rely on holo (ligand-bound) protein conformations for training and evaluation, overlooking the significance of the apo (ligand-free) states.

pmc-12703025.title: Fetus-in-fetu, a rare congenital anomaly: A case report
pmc-12703025.creator: Vida Radi, Nasrin Mohammadi
pmc-12703025.description: BackgroundFetus-in-fetu (FIF) is an extremely rare congenital anomaly characterized by the development of a parasitic fetus within the body of its twin. This condition typically results from abnormal embryogenesis in a monochorionic diamniotic pregnancy. Its incidence is estimated to be approximately 1 in 500,000 live births, with fewer than 200 cases reported in medical literature.

pmc-13253318.title: Acute kidney injury following household pyrethroid aerosol insecticide exposure: a case report and literature review
pmc-13253318.creator: Yuxin Tang, Yuqing Wu, Xuhang Xue, Sihan Tao, Xing Tao, Li Li, Lianyi Geng, Kun Gao, Xufang Wang
pmc-13253318.description: BackgroundPyrethroids (PYRs) are increasingly detected in both environmental matrices and human populations. Emerging evidence underscores their potential for systemic toxicity. Biopsy-confirmed nephrotoxicity in humans remains sparsely documented, particularly in non-occupational exposure. We present a case of acute kidney injury (AKI) associated with household pyrethroid-containing aerosol insecticide exposure.

pmc-13433668.description: BackgroundThe inflammation-immune-nutrition score (IINS) plays a significant role in predicting survival outcomes across various cancers. pmc-13490645.title: Genetic Characterization and Subtype Isolation of Circulating Metapneumovirus in Commercial Turkeys in the Central Region
pmc-13490645.creator: Hosseini Seyed Davood, Mahdavi Morteza, Asli Esmaeil, Lotfi Mohsen
pmc-13490645.description: Introduction: Rhinotracheitis is an acute respiratory infection in turkeys and is considered a relatively significant economic disease caused by Avian metapneumovirus (AMPV) in poultry species. AMPV is responsible for turkey rhinotracheitis (TRT) and swollen head syndrome (SHS) in chickens, which is usually accompanied by secondary bacterial infections that increase mortality.
